brief.headline: A cold week, Black Friday noise and year-end recaps: show warm, finished rooms and let the free 3D studio do the selling.
brief.summary: Three things are moving at once. Ofgem confirmed yesterday that the energy price cap rises 26% from 1 January, in the coldest week of the autumn so far, so warm-bathroom content has a real reason to exist today. Black Friday is tomorrow and 71% of UK adults doubt the discounts are genuine, which makes a calm 'no fake discounts, just your room priced to the pound' message stand out. On Reels and TikTok, same-angle before/after cuts and 'finished result first' hooks are beating account averages by 9 to 14 times, and year-end recap formats are rising fast. Lead with the studio: a priced, photographed room in minutes is the most shareable thing this brand owns.

trends.name: Same-angle before/after, cut on the beat
trends.what_it_is: Lock the camera in one spot at strip-out, then cut to the finished room from the identical angle on the beat drop.
trends.why_now: Volume's home and real estate tracker (25 Nov 2026, 995 posts) ranks it the top home format: 14 accounts at a median 14x their usual reach, with one 1920s bathroom makeover reveal at 50x.
trends.how_we_use_it: Pair the studio render with the fitted room from the same angle: 'the picture you approved' then 'the room we fitted'. Exactly the brand promise.

trends.name: Finished result flashed before the process
trends.what_it_is: Two seconds of the finished room up front, then back to the start to show how it got there.
trends.why_now: Top home and real estate format measured on 25 Nov 2026: 20 accounts at a median 9x their usual reach.
trends.how_we_use_it: Open every studio screen recording on the finished render, then show the three choices that made it.

trends.name: Energy price cap up 26% from January, in a cold snap
trends.what_it_is: Ofgem's 25 Nov announcement: typical dual-fuel bill from £1,723 to £2,166 a year from 1 January, gas up 33%, electricity up 19%. The Met Office forecast below-average temperatures and hill snow risk this week.
trends.why_now: Announced yesterday and leading UK news in the coldest week so far.
trends.how_we_use_it: Warm-bathroom content without scaremongering: towel rails on timers, underfloor heating controls, insulation behind tiles. No running-cost figures until recalculated at January rates.

trends.name: Black Friday scepticism
trends.what_it_is: Black Friday is Friday 27 November. Barclays (23 Nov) found 71% of UK adults question whether discounts are genuine and 72% say it is more marketing than sales.
trends.why_now: Peak noise from today to Cyber Monday (30 Nov). Chatfuel also spotted a 'Black Friday story reveal' format this week: a 10 to 15 second mini-story that hides the brand until the last frame.
trends.how_we_use_it: Counter-programme calmly: no countdowns, no 'was' prices, just a real room priced to the pound with VAT. Talk about our approach, never about competitors.

trends.name: 'I feel like I haven't done much this year' recap
trends.what_it_is: Open on the line, then fast month-by-month clips as proof. Usual audio: 'Coming Up Roses' by Harry Styles.
trends.why_now: SocialPilot: the audio went from 49K to 116K Reels in under three weeks; Later added it on 20 Nov. Year-end reflection season runs to mid-December.
trends.how_we_use_it: 'We feel like we haven't done much this year' then twelve rooms, designs or deliveries, one per month. Check the song is available on a business account; otherwise use original audio with the same structure.

trends.name: Slow festive walk-through ('Christmas Market', Eoneun)
trends.what_it_is: A calm, textless glide through a decorated space, set to the instrumental 'Christmas Market' by Eoneun.
trends.why_now: SocialPilot: from 72K to 89K Reels in three days; Postdom counts 106K and marks it trending.
trends.how_we_use_it: Ten seconds through a finished bathroom styled for Christmas at dusk. The most premium of this season's formats.

trends.name: Contrarian bathroom rules
trends.what_it_is: A one-line rejection of a popular choice ('Unpopular opinion: spotlights ruin bathrooms'), then the reason and the better option.
trends.why_now: UK interiors creators' top bathroom posts this month are 'don't' tips (against spotlights 513K views, against black taps 416K views, Modash, 25 Nov). Volume: 'reject a popular trend in one line' at a median 5x across 13 accounts.
trends.how_we_use_it: A designer says one rule to camera and shows the alternative in the studio. Backed by the Sanctuary 2027 survey: matt black brassware and fluted everything are losing momentum, layered lighting is the top designer forecast.

trends.name: Hard calendar deadline as the hook
trends.what_it_is: A countdown or fixed date in the first line ('29 days until Christmas guests').
trends.why_now: Volume (25 Nov): median 16x across 7 home accounts. Hosting season: 59% of hosts say more people use their bathroom over the holidays (Talker Research, 19 Nov, US).
trends.how_we_use_it: Guest-bathroom quick wins now, with the real renovation designed over Christmas and fitted in the new year.

trends.name: 'In this town everybody goes out partying except me'
trends.what_it_is: Voiceover about everyone partying while the creator works, with a 'huss' sound effect.
trends.why_now: Virlo: up 6050% in creators week on week; Postdom counts 528,900 videos on the sound.
trends.how_we_use_it: The 6 am van load, setting-out lines and a tiler at work, ending on the finished room. Light, human, shows the craft.

trends.name: YouTube Shorts: custom thumbnails and seasons
trends.what_it_is: Every creator can now upload a custom Shorts thumbnail (announced 23 Nov), and Shorts can be grouped into seasons and episodes.
trends.why_now: Rolled out this week. Volume finds episode numbers in titles earn a median 12x for home accounts.
trends.how_we_use_it: One consistent 'finished room' cover per Short and a 'Screen to Room' season, so the Shorts shelf reads like a portfolio.

ideas.title: Same room. £5k, £15k, £50k.
ideas.trend: Finished result flashed before the process
ideas.concept: One real room run through the 3D studio three times: £5,000, £15,000 and £50,000, same mood and finish. Flash all three finished renders first and ask viewers to guess, then reveal the budgets and what changed between them. It turns the studio into a game and ends on the only action that matters: set your own budget.
ideas.why_it_works: It uses the top-performing home hook this week (finished result first) and invites comments (guesses), which feed reach. It also answers the question every homeowner has ('what does my budget actually buy?') and shows the studio doing it in seconds, free.

reel.audio: Original audio: a soft piano or ambient bed with a light tick on each reveal. If you want a trending sound, pick an instrumental from the in-app business library.

ideas.title: Warm bathroom, sensible bills
ideas.trend: Energy price cap up 26% from January, in a cold snap
ideas.hook: Energy bills rise 26% in January. Your bathroom doesn't have to be the coldest room in the house.
ideas.concept: A calm, useful carousel on keeping a bathroom warm without wasting heat: towel rails on timers, underfloor heating controls, insulated boards behind tiles, the right extractor, and designing heating in from the start. Ends on designing it in 3D with heating included in the price.
ideas.why_it_works: It is the most talked-about household story in the UK this week and the coldest days so far. Carousels lead Instagram engagement in 2026 (Buffer: 6.9% vs 3.3% for Reels), and practical lists get saved and sent.

slides.headline: Bills rise 26% in January.
slides.body: Here's how to keep your bathroom warm without heating the whole house.
slides.visual: Steam on a stone basin at dusk, warm light. Cream text on navy band.

slides.headline: Put the towel rail on a timer
slides.body: Twenty minutes before your shower is all it needs. A thermostatic or smart element stops it running all day.
slides.visual: Heated towel rail with folded towels, close-up of the control

slides.headline: Underfloor heating, set properly
slides.body: Wet systems run from your boiler or heat pump; electric mats suit single rooms. Either way, a programmable thermostat does the saving.
slides.visual: Bare feet on warm tiles, morning light

slides.headline: Insulate behind the tiles
slides.body: On an outside wall, insulated tile backer boards keep heat in the room instead of the brickwork.
slides.visual: Fitter fixing backer boards, before tiling

slides.headline: Ventilate without the draught
slides.body: A humidity-sensing extractor clears steam and switches off when the air is dry.
slides.visual: Ceiling extractor in a finished room, clean lines

slides.headline: Design heating in from day one
slides.body: In our studio the rail, the floor and the controls are priced with everything else, inside your budget.
slides.visual: Studio render with the towel rail and heating tagged

slides.headline: See yours warm, before you buy

ideas.why_it_works: Rides the Black Friday story-reveal format while siding with the 71% who doubt the discounts. It positions the brand as the calm, honest choice without naming anyone.

ideas.title: The quiet glide: a bathroom dressed for Christmas
ideas.hook: No words. Just the first warm bath of December.
ideas.concept: A ten-second, textless slow pan through a finished bathroom at dusk: eucalyptus over the shower, candles on stone, warm towels on the rail, steam rising from a freestanding bath. One caption line does the talking.
ideas.why_it_works: The calm festive walk-through is rising fast on Reels and suits a premium brand far better than loud Christmas trends. Saves and sends follow beautiful rooms.

reel.audio: 'Christmas Market' by Eoneun if it shows in the business audio library (it is an instrumental, so it often does); otherwise a royalty-free music-box instrumental.

ideas.title: Unpopular opinion: spotlights are why your bathroom feels like a clinic
ideas.hook: Unpopular opinion: spotlights are why your bathroom feels like a clinic.
ideas.concept: A designer to camera, one rule, one reason, one better option: layer the light. A lit mirror at face height, a wall light or two, a low glow under the vanity. Then the studio shows the same room lit both ways.
ideas.why_it_works: Contrarian, specific bathroom tips are the top-performing UK interiors posts this month. Layered lighting is the strongest designer forecast for 2027 (86% in the Sanctuary survey), so the advice is credible as well as clickable.

ideas.title: 29 days until Christmas guests: the 20-minute bathroom fixes

ideas.hook: 29 days until the in-laws use your bathroom. Here's what to fix first.
ideas.concept: A save-worthy checklist of quick fixes before Christmas guests arrive (fresh silicone, grout refresh, a new shower head, warm towels, a lamp instead of the big light), ending honestly: the full renovation is a January job, so design it now and book the fit for the new year.
ideas.why_it_works: Deadline hooks are earning a median 16x for home accounts. The 'comment for the list' mechanic earns DMs, which Instagram rewards, and every DM is a warm lead for January.

ideas.title: 6 am: in this town everybody goes out partying except us
ideas.trend: 'In this town everybody goes out partying except me'
ideas.hook: In this town everybody goes out partying except me.
ideas.concept: The fastest-rising TikTok meme, played straight by a fitter: 6 am van load, laser level lines on a bare wall, a tile set into place, the silicone bead, then a hard cut to the finished room. Human, funny, and it shows the craft.
ideas.why_it_works: Creators on the format rose 6050% week on week, so the window is now. Behind-the-scenes from real fitters builds trust in the 'fitted by our own team' promise.

reel.audio: The trending 'in this town' original sound on TikTok (check it is allowed for business use); on Instagram, re-record the line as original audio.

reel.edit_notes: Keep it under 15 seconds. Do not show a client's home or address without permission.

ideas.caption:
In this town everybody goes out partying except us. Someone's got to set out the tiles.

Designed, supplied and fitted by one team.
ideas.production: Film on a live job across a morning (with the client's written permission). Phone in the van, a clamp on the ladder. About 30 minutes of capture, 1 hour edit. Post within the week while the meme is live.

watch_outs: Music: most commercial songs (Harry Styles, Wham!, Mariah Carey) are unavailable to business accounts. Check the in-app audio picker before building a post around a named song; original audio is always safe.
Energy content: do not publish towel rail or underfloor heating running costs. Published figures pre-date the January 2027 cap and conflict; recalculate first.
Black Friday: talk about our approach, never imply competitors' discounts are fake (ASA and CAP Code).
Small Business Saturday UK is Saturday 5 December, not 28 November (that is the US date).
Before/after and recap reels: real projects only, with written client permission; label studio designs as designs.
Facebook: Meta is limiting link posts for Pages; post natively and put the studio link in the first comment.
Prices shown on screen must match the website, VAT included.
